examples.en: An internal inspection of the police has begun.
The results of the inspection will be announced next week.

examples.ko: 감찰을 받은 직원은 잠시 일을 쉬었어요.
examples.en: The employee who was investigated took a short break from work.

examples.ko: 학교 안의 문제를 감찰하는 부서가 따로 있어요.
examples.en: There is a separate department that inspects problems inside the school.
The inspector came to check the documents.

examples.ko: 군대에서는 규칙을 지키는지 감찰을 자주 해요.
examples.en: In the military, they often inspect whether rules are followed.

explain: 공공기관, 군대, 경찰 같은 조직 안에서 규칙을 어기지 않았는지 살펴보는 일에 써요. '감사'는 돈과 업무 전체를 살피는 데 많이 쓰고, 감찰은 사람의 행동과 근무 태도를 살피는 데 써요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to checking, inside public bodies, the military or the police, whether people have broken rules. 감사 (audit) is often about money and overall work, while 감찰 looks at people's conduct and work attitude. It rarely comes up in everyday conversation.

examples.en: The law was revised this year.
The textbook was newly revised.
Be sure to read the revised rules.
I will send a text when the price list is revised.
The exam system is being revised.
The terms were revised, so I got a notification.

explain: '개정'은 법·규칙·책의 내용을 고치는 것이에요. 있는 법을 고칠 때는 '개정', 없던 법을 새로 만들 때는 '제정'이에요. 서점에서 보이는 '개정판'은 고쳐서 다시 낸 책이에요. 소리가 비슷한 '개선'(더 좋게 고침)과 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: '개정' is changing the content of laws, rules, or books. Changing an existing law is '개정', while making a new one is '제정'. In bookstores, '개정판' is a revised edition. Do not confuse it with the similar-sounding '개선' (improvement).

examples.en: Under the building code, the height of buildings is restricted.

examples.ko: 건축법을 어기고 집을 지으면 벌금을 내야 해요.
examples.en: If you build a house against the building laws, you have to pay a fine.
The new building law takes effect next month.

examples.ko: 건축법이 바뀌어서 설계를 다시 해야 했어요.
examples.en: The building law changed, so we had to redo the design.

examples.ko: 건축법 때문에 이 땅에는 높은 건물을 지을 수 없어요.
examples.en: Because of the building law, you can't build a tall building on this land.
An architect must know the building laws well too.

explain: 건물을 지을 때 지켜야 할 높이, 안전, 구조 같은 규칙을 정한 법이에요. 뉴스와 부동산 이야기에서 '건축법에 따라', '건축법을 위반하다'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the law that sets the rules for building, such as height, safety and structure. It often appears in news and real-estate talk in phrases like '건축법에 따라' and '건축법을 위반하다'.

examples.en: The military used to inspect letters too.

examples.ko: 정부가 책의 내용을 검열한다는 소문이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a rumor that the government censors the content of books.

examples.ko: 방송국은 영상을 먼저 검열한 다음에 내보내요.
examples.en: The broadcaster censors the video first and then airs it.

examples.ko: 학교에서 학생들의 일기를 검열하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: A school must not inspect students' diaries.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 신문 기사를 검열해서 일부를 지웠어요.
examples.en: In the past, newspaper articles were censored and parts were erased.

examples.ko: 부모님이 제 문자를 검열하는 것 같아서 싫어요.
examples.en: I don't like it, because it seems my parents check my messages.

explain: '검열하다'는 글, 영상, 편지의 내용을 확인해서 문제가 있으면 막거나 지울 때 써요. 단순히 살펴보는 '검사하다'와 다르게 표현의 자유를 누른다는 느낌이 있어요. 군대에서 부대를 점검하는 '검열'은 따로 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: 검열하다 means checking the content of writing, video or letters and blocking or removing what is a problem. Unlike plain 검사하다 (to inspect), it carries a sense of limiting freedom of expression. The military 검열, an inspection of a unit, is a different meaning.

examples.en: I want to get a job at a public enterprise.
A public enterprise is a company owned by the state.
I'm preparing for the public enterprise exam.
They say pay at public enterprises is stable.
That public enterprise started a new business.
My older brother works at a public enterprise.

explain: 한국전력이나 한국철도공사처럼 나라나 지방 정부가 만든 회사예요. 반대말은 '사기업'이에요. 한국에서는 안정적이라서 취업 준비생에게 인기가 많아요.
explain_en: These are companies set up by the state or local government, like the national power or railway corporations. The opposite is 사기업 (private company). In Korea they are popular with job seekers for their stability.

examples.en: A letter came from the National Health Insurance Service.
My father works at a factory in the industrial complex.
This city has a big industrial complex.
A staff member there checked my documents.

examples.ko: 공단 근처는 아침마다 출근 버스가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many commuter buses near the industrial area every morning.
I called the agency and asked about the pension issue.

explain: '공단'은 두 가지로 쓰여요. 기관 이름 끝에 붙으면 나라 일을 하는 공공 기관이고, '공단에 다니다'처럼 지역을 말하면 공장이 모인 곳이에요. 문장에서 어느 쪽인지 보면 구별돼요.
explain_en: It has two uses. At the end of an organization name, such as '국민건강보험공단', it is a public agency doing state work. Used for a place, as in '공단에 다니다' (work at an industrial complex), it means an area where factories are clustered. The sentence tells you which one.

examples.en: The prosecution submitted the indictment to the court.
They say the contents of the indictment were made public on the news.
The lawyer read the indictment carefully.
What charges are written in the indictment?
Once the indictment is filed, the trial begins.
The reporters waited to get a copy of the indictment.

explain: 뉴스에서 재판 소식이 나올 때 자주 들리는 말이에요. 검사가 재판을 청구하며 법원에 내는 서류를 가리키고, '공소장을 제출하다', '공소장이 접수되다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: You often hear this word when trial news is reported. It is the document a prosecutor files with the court to bring a case to trial, used as '공소장을 제출하다' or '공소장이 접수되다'.

examples.ko: 두 회사의 합병이 다음 주에 공식화돼요.
examples.en: The merger of the two companies will be made official next week.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 교제가 공식화됐다는 기사가 나왔어요.
examples.en: An article came out saying the two people's relationship has been made official.

examples.ko: 새로운 규칙이 공식화되면 모두 따라야 해요.
examples.en: Once the new rule is made official, everyone has to follow it.

examples.ko: 구두로 한 약속은 문서로 공식화되어야 효력이 있어요.
examples.en: A verbal promise is only valid once it is formalized in a document.
That plan hasn't been made official yet.

examples.ko: 협력 관계가 공식화된 뒤 서로 자주 만나요.
examples.en: Since the partnership was formalized, they meet each other often.

explain: 소문이나 구두 약속이 발표, 서명, 문서를 통해 '공식'이 될 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '공식화됐다'처럼 과거형으로 많이 나와요. 하는 쪽을 말할 때는 '공식화하다'를 써서 '정부가 계획을 공식화했어요'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when a rumor or verbal promise becomes official through an announcement, signature or document. In the news it often appears in the past tense, like '공식화됐다'. When the doer is stated, use '공식화하다', as in '정부가 계획을 공식화했어요'.

examples.en: The government officially recognized this institution's qualification.

examples.ko: 국제 협회가 그 기록을 공식 기록으로 공인해 줬어요.
examples.en: The international association certified that record as an official one.

examples.ko: 공인된 시험 점수가 있어야 지원할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You need an officially recognized test score to apply.
This certificate is recognized by the state.
He's a top talent that everyone acknowledges.

examples.ko: 협회가 공인하지 않은 대회라서 기록이 안 남아요.
examples.en: It isn't a competition the association recognizes, so no record is kept.

explain: 나라나 큰 기관이 공식적으로 인정할 때 쓰고, '공인 시험', '공인 점수'처럼 명사 앞에도 많이 붙어요. 개인이 인정할 때는 '인정하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it when a state or major institution officially recognizes something, and it often attaches before nouns, as in '공인 시험' (certified exam) and '공인 점수' (certified score). When an individual acknowledges something, use '인정하다'.

dis.h: officially recognize as valid or qualified

p.n: 인가하다 means granting permission to operate, so it does not fit with certifying a record.

examples.en: Our police station has jurisdiction over this area.
Which department is in charge of this matter?

examples.ko: 시청이 관할하는 공원이라서 청소를 자주 해요.
examples.en: It's a park under city hall's management, so it gets cleaned often.
The court will have jurisdiction over that issue.
The area the fire station used to cover changed last year.

examples.ko: 시청에서는 자기들이 관할하지 않는 일은 도와줄 수 없다고 했어요.
examples.en: City hall said it can't help with things outside its jurisdiction.

explain: '맡다'는 일상에서 아무 일에나 쓰지만 관할하다는 경찰서·구청 같은 기관이 권한을 가진 구역이나 업무에만 써요. 보통 '~이/가 관할하다'로 쓰고, 뉴스와 공문서에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: '맡다' (take charge) works for any task, but 관할하다 is only for an agency such as a police station or district office that holds authority over an area or duty. It usually appears as '~이/가 관할하다' in news and official documents.

examples.en: City Hall issues certificates.
The school handed diplomas to the graduates.
They will issue the permit tomorrow morning.
You need an ID to have the documents issued.
The staff member handed over the receipt and then said goodbye.
The documents handed out at the counter are free.

explain: '교부하다'는 관청이나 학교가 공식 서류를 사람에게 내주는 거예요. 같은 뜻으로 '발급하다'를 더 많이 쓰고, 교부하다는 조금 딱딱한 서류 느낌이에요. 일상에서 서류를 받을 때는 '받다'라고 하면 돼요.
explain_en: 교부하다 is when an office or school officially hands a document to someone. 발급하다 is more common, and 교부하다 sounds more bureaucratic. As the receiver in daily life, simply say 받다.

examples.ko: 국공립 어린이집에 들어가려면 오래 기다려야 해요.
examples.en: To get into a public daycare center, you have to wait a long time.

examples.ko: 국공립과 사립 학교는 등록금이 많이 달라요.
examples.en: Tuition differs a lot between public and private schools.

examples.ko: 이 도서관은 국공립이라서 이용료가 거의 없어요.
examples.en: This library is public, so there's hardly any fee to use it.
Public museums are open on Sundays too.
The number of facilities being converted to public ones is growing.
Do you think public ones are safer than private ones?

explain: 국립과 공립을 한꺼번에 묶은 말이라, 뒤에 어린이집, 유치원, 학교, 도서관 같은 시설 이름이 자주 와요. 반대되는 말은 '사립'이에요.
explain_en: It bundles national and public together, so facility names such as daycare, kindergarten, school, and library often follow it. The opposite is '사립' (private).

examples.en: This park was originally state-owned land.
You can't sell state-owned land as you please.

examples.ko: 산 대부분이 국유지라서 개인이 집을 지을 수 없어요.
examples.en: Most of the mountain is state-owned, so individuals can't build houses.

examples.ko: 국유지에 허락 없이 밭을 만들면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not make a field on state land without permission.

examples.ko: 정부가 국유지 일부를 시민에게 빌려주기로 했어요.
examples.en: The government decided to lend part of its land to citizens.

examples.ko: 이 땅이 국유지인지 사유지인지 확인해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's check whether this land is state-owned or private.

explain: 나라가 가진 땅을 말하고, 개인이 가진 '사유지'와 짝으로 자주 나와요. 땅을 빌리거나 집을 지을 때, 또 뉴스에서 이 말을 들을 수 있어요. 시나 도가 가진 땅은 '공유지'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It means land owned by the state, and it often pairs with '사유지' (private land). You may hear it when renting land, building a house, or in the news. Land owned by a city or province is also called '공유지' (public land).

examples.ko: 새로운 법 때문에 광고가 많이 규제돼요.
examples.en: Advertising is heavily regulated because of the new law.

examples.ko: 어린이 대상 광고는 엄격하게 규제되고 있어요.
examples.en: Ads aimed at children are strictly restricted.

examples.ko: 이 지역에서는 드론 비행이 규제된 적이 있어요.
examples.en: Drone flights were once restricted in this area.

examples.ko: 가격이 규제되면 가게 주인들이 힘들어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If prices are regulated, shop owners may struggle.

examples.ko: 뉴스에 따르면 내년부터 수입이 더 규제될 거예요.
examples.en: According to the news, imports will be more restricted starting next year.

examples.ko: 규제되는 분야에서는 허가를 먼저 받아야 해요.
examples.en: In regulated fields, you have to get a permit first.

explain: 주로 법이나 정부 같은 공적인 힘이 무엇을 제한할 때 써요. 일상에서 내가 스스로 참는 것에는 잘 안 써요. 하는 쪽을 말하려면 '규제하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used when laws or authorities limit something, mostly in news and formal talk. It is not used for holding yourself back in daily life. To name who does the regulating, use the active verb 규제하다.

en: dismiss; reject (a court case or appeal)

examples.en: The court rejected his request.
The judge dismissed the lawsuit, and it was on the news.

examples.ko: 이번에도 재판부가 신청을 기각할 것 같아요.
examples.en: The court seems likely to reject the application again.
What was the reason for dismissing the appeal?

examples.ko: 법원이 기각하면 신청한 사람이 결과를 문서로 받아요.
examples.en: If the court dismisses it, the applicant receives the result in writing.
The lawyer hoped the court would not dismiss it.

explain: 법원이 따져 본 뒤 요청을 받아들이지 않을 때 써요. 내용을 보지 않고 돌려보내는 것은 '각하', 요청을 받아들이는 것은 '인용하다'예요. 일상에서 거절할 때는 '거절하다'를 써요. 뉴스와 재판 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when a court examines a request and turns it down. Throwing it out without looking at the content is 각하, and accepting it is 인용하다. In daily life you refuse with 거절하다. You meet it in news and trial stories.

en: be based on; be founded on

examples.en: This movie is based on a true story.
You have to write something based on facts.
The plan was based on the survey results.
I'll speak based on my experience.
We decided on the basis of the law.

examples.ko: 자료에 기초하지 않은 주장은 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: A claim not based on data is hard to believe.

explain: '기초하다'는 항상 '~에 기초하다'로 써요. 조사 '에'를 빠뜨리지 마세요. '기초한'처럼 꾸미는 모양으로 '사실에 기초한 이야기'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: 기초하다 is always used as '~에 기초하다' (be based on ~), so don't drop the particle 에. The modifier form is common, as in '사실에 기초한 이야기' (a story based on facts).

en: resident of a province (such as Gyeonggi-do or Jeju-do)

examples.ko: 도민들이 새 공항 건설에 대해 의견을 냈어요.
examples.en: The province's residents gave their opinions on building the new airport.
Most of the province's residents were in favor of this plan.
This event is open free of charge to the province's residents.
The provincial governor said they would listen to the residents' voices.

examples.ko: 도민을 위한 문화 공간이 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new cultural space for the province's residents has opened.

examples.ko: 도민 설문 조사에서 교통이 가장 큰 문제로 나왔어요.
examples.en: In the survey of residents, transportation came out as the biggest problem.

explain: 경기도, 충청북도, 제주도처럼 '도'에 사는 사람을 '도민'이라고 해요. 시에 사는 사람은 '시민', 군에 사는 사람은 '군민', 구에 사는 사람은 '구민'이에요. '제주도민'처럼 지역 이름 뒤에 붙여 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: People who live in a '도' (province), such as Gyeonggi-do, Chungcheongbuk-do or Jeju-do, are called '도민'. Those living in a '시' are '시민', in a '군' are '군민', and in a '구' are '구민'. It is often attached to a region name, as in '제주도민'.

examples.en: When you buy a house, you have to register ownership.

examples.ko: 땅을 산 뒤에 바로 등기하고 서류를 받았어요.
examples.en: I registered the land right after buying it and received the documents.
How much does it cost to register it?
This building hasn't been registered yet.
I'm going to register it in my father's name.
Once you set up a company, you just register it first.

explain: 집이나 땅을 샀을 때 소유자를 나라 기록에 올리는 일에 써요. 일상 대화보다 계약이나 부동산 이야기에서 들어요. 우편은 '등기로 보내다'처럼 '하다' 없이 말해요.
explain_en: Used when an owner is entered into the official record after buying a house or land. You hear it in contracts and real-estate talk rather than daily chat. For mail, Koreans say 등기로 보내다 without 하다.

examples.ko: 구청에서 이사 간 사람의 주소를 말소해요.
examples.en: The district office strikes the address of people who have moved away.
After scrapping the car, I cancelled its registration.

examples.ko: 잘못 적은 기록은 말소하고 다시 쓰세요.
examples.en: Strike out the wrongly written record and write it again.

examples.ko: 회사는 연락이 안 되는 회원의 계정을 말소하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The company decided to delete the accounts of members who can't be reached.

examples.ko: 세무서가 사업자 등록을 말소하면 영업을 할 수 없어요.
examples.en: If the tax office cancels your business registration, you can't operate.

examples.ko: 명단에서 제 이름을 말소해 달라고 부탁했어요.
examples.en: I asked them to remove my name from the list.

explain: 등록이나 기록을 공식적으로 없앨 때 써요. 글자를 지우개로 지우는 일은 '지우다'가 자연스러워요. '삭제하다'는 컴퓨터 파일에도 쓰지만 '말소하다'는 주로 등록이나 명단에 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a registration or record is officially removed. For erasing writing, '지우다' sounds more natural. '삭제하다' also works for computer files, while '말소하다' is mostly for registrations and lists.

examples.en: I went to the township office to get a document.
The township office helps villagers with their affairs.
A township office worker explained kindly.
Grandmother applied for her pension at the township office.

examples.ko: 우리 마을 면사무소는 오후 여섯 시에 문을 닫아요.
examples.en: The township office in our village closes at six in the evening.

examples.ko: 이사를 하면 면사무소에서 주소를 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: After moving, you have to change your address at the township office.

explain: '면사무소'는 시골의 '면'이라는 지역 단위 행정 기관이에요. 도시에서는 같은 일을 '주민센터'에서 해요. 면보다 큰 '읍'에는 '읍사무소'가 있어요.
explain_en: '면사무소' is the local government office of a '면', a rural area unit. In cities the same work is done at a '주민센터'. A '읍', which is larger than a '면', has an '읍사무소'.

examples.en: Subway fares are waived for people aged 65 and over.
There are many places where admission is free for children.

examples.ko: 성적이 좋으면 수업료가 면제될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If your grades are good, your tuition can be waived.
I was exempted from this exam because of an illness.
If I submit the documents, will the tax be waived?
Parking fees are waived at this hour, which is convenient.

explain: 내야 할 돈이나 해야 할 의무를 안 해도 되게 해 주는 것이에요. 혜택을 받는 쪽은 '면제되다' 또는 '면제받다'를 쓰고, 해 주는 쪽은 '면제하다'를 써요. '수면제'의 '면제'와는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It means being let off from money you owe or a duty you must do. The receiving side uses '면제되다' or '면제받다', and the giving side uses '면제하다'. It is a different word from '면제' in '수면제' (sleeping pill).

examples.ko: 무면허로 운전하다가 사고가 나서 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: He had an accident while driving without a license and it was on the news.

examples.ko: 친구가 무면허 운전은 절대 안 된다고 말했어요.
examples.en: My friend said driving without a license is absolutely not allowed.

examples.ko: 무면허 상태에서 차를 빌려주면 큰일 나요.
examples.en: You'll be in big trouble if you lend your car to someone without a license.

examples.ko: 저 가게는 무면허 업소라서 문을 닫았대요.
examples.en: I heard that shop was closed because it was operating without a license.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 무면허인 줄 모르고 차를 탔어요.
examples.en: I got in the car without knowing he had no license.

examples.ko: 요즘 무면허 오토바이 사고가 자주 일어나요.
examples.en: Accidents involving unlicensed motorcycle riders happen often these days.

explain: 대부분 '무면허 운전', '무면허 운전자'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여 써요. 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 많이 나오고, 반대로 면허가 있을 때는 '면허가 있다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used before another noun, as in '무면허 운전' (unlicensed driving) or '무면허 운전자'. It appears often in news and legal talk; for the opposite, people just say '면허가 있다' (to have a license).

examples.ko: 시행 첫날부터 시청 민원실에 문의 전화가 몰렸어요.
examples.en: From the first day it took effect, inquiry calls flooded the city hall service office.

examples.ko: 민원실에서 서류를 발급받으면 관인이 선명하게 찍혔는지 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: When you get a document at the service office, check that the official seal is clearly stamped.
Until what time is the service office open?
The service office counters were very crowded.
A service office staff member kindly explained it to me.

examples.ko: 민원실로 가시면 바로 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go to the service office, you can apply right away.

explain: 시청, 구청, 주민센터에서 증명서를 떼거나 신청을 하는 곳이에요. 등본이나 증명서 이야기를 할 때 자주 나와요. 대화에서는 그냥 '구청 가서 뗐어요'처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the place in a city hall, ward office or community center where you get certificates or file requests. It often comes up when talking about resident registration copies or other certificates. In conversation people may just say '구청 가서 뗐어요' (I went to the ward office and got it).

en: deprive of; strip (a right or title)

examples.en: The court stripped him of his qualification.

examples.ko: 아무도 아이의 학습권을 박탈할 수 없어요.
examples.en: No one can take away a child's right to learn.

examples.ko: 규정을 어긴 선수의 메달을 박탈하기로 했어요.
examples.en: They decided to strip the medal from the athlete who broke the rules.

examples.ko: 기회를 박탈하는 것은 너무 가혹한 일이에요.
examples.en: Depriving someone of the chance is far too harsh.
The company took away their rights, so the employees protested.

examples.ko: 남의 자유를 박탈하면 큰 벌을 받아요.
examples.en: If you take away someone's freedom, you get a heavy penalty.

explain: 박탈하다는 권리, 자격, 자유를 힘으로 빼앗을 때 쓰는 말이에요. 물건을 빼앗을 때는 '빼앗다'를 쓰고, 박탈하다는 '권리', '자격', '기회' 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 당하는 쪽에서는 '박탈당하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when rights, qualifications or freedom are taken away by force or by authority. For taking physical objects, 빼앗다 is used, and 박탈하다 pairs with abstract nouns such as 권리, 자격 and 기회. From the victim's side, there is 박탈당하다.

examples.en: The government will promulgate the new law tomorrow.
The king proclaimed the new script to his people.

examples.ko: 법을 반포할 날짜가 아직 정해지지 않았어요.
examples.en: The date to promulgate the law has not been set yet.
They made the day the constitution was promulgated a holiday.

examples.ko: 관청에서 새 규칙을 반포하고 안내문도 붙였어요.
examples.en: The office announced the new rule and also put up a notice.

examples.ko: 시장님이 새 조례를 반포해서 모두 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: The mayor proclaimed the new ordinance, so everyone found out.

explain: 반포하다는 나라나 관청이 법, 문자, 새 제도를 공식적으로 세상에 알릴 때만 써요. 일상에서 소식을 전할 때는 '알리다', '발표하다'를 써요. '법을 반포하다', '헌법을 반포하다'처럼 법이나 문자와 같이 나와요.
explain_en: Use it only when a state or office officially makes a law, script or new system public. For everyday news, use 알리다 or 발표하다. It pairs with laws and scripts, as in '법을 반포하다' and '헌법을 반포하다'.

examples.en: The court decided to issue the warrant.
It takes some time until a warrant is issued.
Issuing the permit is handled by the district office.

examples.ko: 영장 발부 절차는 법으로 정해져 있어요.
examples.en: The procedure for issuing a warrant is set by law.
Whether the warrant is issued will be decided tomorrow.
The bill was issued late, so the payment got delayed.

explain: 증명서나 서류는 보통 '발급'이라고 하고, '발부'는 영장·허가증·고지서처럼 공적인 기관이 법적 효력이 있는 것을 내줄 때 많이 써요. 두 말이 비슷해 보여도 '영장 발부'처럼 굳은 짝이 있어요. 책이나 돈을 내는 것은 '발행'이에요.
explain_en: Certificates and documents are usually '발급', while '발부' is often used when an official body issues something with legal force, like a warrant, permit or bill. The two look similar, but there are fixed pairings like '영장 발부'. Issuing books or money is '발행'.

en: fine (monetary penalty imposed as a sentence)

examples.en: He was fined and released.
It was a minor accident, so it ended with a fine.
I saw news that the court ordered a fine.

examples.ko: 잘못이 크지 않으면 벌금형에 그칠 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If the wrong isn't serious, it may end with a fine.

examples.ko: 벌금형 처분을 받은 사람은 기한 안에 돈을 내야 해요.
examples.en: A person given a fine must pay within the deadline.
A fine is generally lighter than a prison sentence.

explain: '벌금'은 내야 하는 돈이고, '벌금형'은 법원이 판결로 정한 벌을 말해요. 감옥에 가는 '징역형'과 비교해서 자주 써요. 교통 위반처럼 가벼운 일에는 '범칙금'이나 '과태료'라는 말을 써요.
explain_en: 벌금 is the money to be paid, while 벌금형 is the punishment a court decides in its ruling. It is often compared with 징역형, which means going to prison. For light matters like traffic violations, the words 범칙금 and 과태료 are used.

en: serve (in the military or public service)

examples.ko: 오빠는 일 년 반 동안 군대에서 복무했어요.
examples.en: My older brother served in the army for a year and a half.
He is currently serving in the navy.

examples.ko: 군대에서 복무하면서 요리를 배웠다는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people say they learned to cook while serving in the army.
Those who will serve as social service personnel, please come this way.

examples.ko: 국경 근처 부대에서 복무해서 눈을 자주 봤어요.
examples.en: I served at a unit near the border, so I saw snow often.

examples.ko: 같은 부대에서 복무하던 친구를 우연히 만났어요.
examples.en: I ran into a friend who served in the same unit.

explain: 한국에서는 군대 이야기에서 가장 많이 나와요. '군 복무', '복무 기간'처럼 명사로도 써요. 회사에서 일할 때는 '근무하다'를 써서 '회사에서 근무하다'라고 해요. 복무하다는 병역 같은 의무의 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: In Korea it comes up most in talk about the military, and also as a noun in '군 복무' (military service) and '복무 기간' (service period). For working at a company, use 근무하다, as in '회사에서 근무하다'. 복무하다 carries the feel of a duty like military service.

examples.en: If you speed, a fine may be imposed.

examples.ko: 이번 달부터 이 상품에 새 세금이 부과되었어요.
examples.en: A new tax has been levied on this product since this month.
A high tax will be imposed on the company.
Please check whether the amount charged is correct.
A heavy responsibility was placed on the team leader.
The fee is charged according to the amount used.

explain: 부과되다는 세금·벌금·요금·책임이 정해져서 사람이나 회사에게 지워질 때 쓰는 말이에요. 정하는 쪽(나라·회사)은 '부과하다'이고 받는 쪽은 '부과되다'예요. 일상에서 요금은 '나오다', '내야 하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: 부과되다 is used when a tax, fine, fee or responsibility is set and placed on a person or company. The authority that sets it says '부과하다', and the one who gets it says '부과되다'. In daily life a bill may simply be '나오다' or '내야 하다'.
